public_rationale: On the ordinary annual-budget reading supplied by the surrounding discussion, the word each overstates the spending. Meta's entire 2025 capital budget was $64–72 billion; its data-center component could not exceed that ceiling on the same definition. That is materially below nearly $100 billion. This contradicts the spending component. It does not establish AI profitability or resolve the opinion that the investments had no real reason.
limitations: The result depends on reading the amount as an annual 2025 budget.
The decisive data-center figure is a derived upper bound, not a disclosed standalone budget.
The upper bound does not cover differently defined multiyear lease commitments.
Nearly is interpreted in its ordinary sense; the speaker supplied no tolerance.

our_interpretation: In the surrounding annual-capex discussion, I read the amount as the 2025 spending budgets known at publication, rather than spending already completed by July.
The principal companies are Amazon, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta. The word each makes the amount a company-by-company assertion.
Nearly $100 billion means close to that amount, not merely tens of billions. No precise tolerance was supplied.
Data-center infrastructure includes its computing equipment. A company's total capital budget provides an upper bound for this component when measured on the same basis.
The lack-of-profit language is separately unresolved; for no real reason is an evaluative judgment rather than a measurable financial result.
Microsoft uses a fiscal year ending in June; the other principal companies use calendar years.
criteria.support_condition: Each principal company's 2025 data-center infrastructure budget, as known at publication, is close to $100 billion. Supporting the profit component additionally requires attributable AI financial results.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one principal company's comparable data-center budget, or a valid upper bound on it, is materially below nearly $100 billion. This would contradict the each assertion without settling the profit or value judgment.
